runtimeImportProof.method: Match captured IAT addresses against named export RVAs of the provided MSVBVM50.dll at one consistent load base. 220 name/slot matches in the scanned region; no DLL loaded or executed.
runtimeImportProof.limitation: The supplied DLL is packed (.textbss has zero raw bytes). Export metadata is readable, but this analysis does not claim to disassemble its unpacked helper bodies from disk. Export-name matching establishes helper identities; helper implementations themselves are not claimed to have been executed or recovered here.

effectiveStats.rounding: VB Int/floor, not round-to-nearest. Divisor at VA 0x40cd70 is an IEEE754 double 100.0.

perTick: a = hero.attack - effectiveDefense; b = effectiveAttack - hero.defense
If a >= 0, monster.battleHp = max(0, monster.battleHp - a); if a < 0, do not heal or damage monster.
If b >= 0, hero.hp = max(0, hero.hp - b); if b < 0, do not heal or damage hero.
There is no monster-death branch between these two updates. The lethal player strike still receives the same tick enemy strike.
If a <= 0 AND b <= 0, apply the stalemate fallback below.
Only after both updates (and rendering/UI checks) test both remaining HP values; if either is zero, switch to the settlement stage.

ordinaryClosedForm.conditions: a > 0; stable hero stats and percent; no interruption; apply special settlement effects separately

example.evidenceType: derived from decoded native operations, not an observed live execution

stalemate.perTickDamage: largest T in {1,10,100,1000,10000} with both CURRENT remaining HP >= T; default T=1
stalemate.updates: Subtract T from both current HP values and clamp each at 0.

settlement.gate: hero.hp > 0 at 0x175547b/0x175547e; hero death does not enter reward block
settlement.afterEffects: hero.hp = max(1, hero.hp), RVA 0x17555a3..0x17555ae; effects do not kill an already-victorious hero
settlement.rewards: hero.gold += monster.goldReward; hero.experience += monster.experienceReward. No percentage multiplier at these additions.
settlement.simultaneousZero: Monster tile is cleared when its HP is zero, even if hero HP is also zero; reward gate requires hero HP > 0. See distinct clear and death checks.
settlement.phaseFlow: Battle begins with counter -5 and interval 70; counter zero selects interval 350; damage ticks use interval 30/300; either HP zero selects 360; phase360 sets counter 1 and interval70; phase70 counter >=5 enters settlement. Interval fields are also acting as stage selectors.

preflight.guard: Only runs normal attack/HP rejection when int16(board + 0xf4) == 0; semantic name of this mode flag not proven.
preflight.attackRejection: baseDefense >= hero.attack normally refuses; uses BASE defense, not percent-adjusted defense.
preflight.hpPrediction: For baseAttack > hero.defense and positive hero.attack-baseDefense: q=baseHp/(hero.attack-baseDefense); n=Int(q); if q>n then n=n+1; predictedDamage=n*(baseAttack-hero.defense).
preflight.hpRejection: predictedDamage > hero.hp normally refuses; equality is not rejected here.
preflight.exception: mapCode==70 AND current floor variant [0x224b1d8]==21 bypasses these rejection paths.

messages.0x5cf798: Monster considers your combat ability too low and refuses battle.
messages.0x5cf7c4: Monster considers your HP too low and refuses battle.

preflight.limitation: This admission estimate omits percent scaling and the four settlement effects; it is not the authoritative damage routine.

unknowns: Monster display names not proven from native text-to-record mapping; null names are intentional.
BattleHp and battleMapCellIndex raw values immediately after new-game initialization are not proven. Their battle-entry assignments are proven.
Full UI/mode meaning of board+0xf4 and flag 0x224d728 is outside this analysis; preserve the branch conditions rather than naming a difficulty mode.
All numeric formulas assume the native signed-32-bit arithmetic stays in range. Native jo branches raise VB overflow; a port must not silently wrap.
No original executable or DLL was run. Runtime behavior claims above are static control/data-flow derivations, not playthrough verification.
